description: Looks up to 20 product identifiers in one call: barcodes (EAN/UPC/GTIN), Amazon ASINs, WEM IDs, catalogue slugs or wem3.ai/pl URLs. Each row has a status: found (WEM's catalogue holds it; the row gives its number of retailer offers, the lowest current price at a named retailer in the shopper's currency, a marketplace low where there is one, and a link to WEM's product page), not_found (WEM does not hold it yet, which says nothing about whether it exists or has a price), unrecognised (not an identifier, such as a product name) or not_checked (not reached in this call, so not a miss). Identifiers beyond 20 are counted in `overLimit`.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for the shopper's market. Default GBP. Lowest prices are quoted in this currency only, never converted; a product WEM holds only in another currency comes back found with lowPrice null and heldInCurrencies set.

identifiers.description: 1-20 barcodes (EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8, GTIN-14), Amazon ASINs, WEM IDs, catalogue slugs or wem3.ai/pl URLs. Mixed kinds are fine; a comma-separated string is also accepted. Duplicates are looked up once. Each entry must be the identifier alone: not a product name, and not a name with a barcode in it.

name: lookup_products

outputSchema.description: One row per distinct identifier, in the order sent. A row is a catalogue fact, not an offer: it says whether WEM holds the product and what the lowest price is, and links to WEM’s product page. Call compare_offers with product.slug for the retailer offers and their links.

overLimit.description: Identifiers beyond the per-call limit, not looked up.

disclosure.description: WEM’s affiliate disclosure for this answer, written to be quoted as it is. Its wording changes with the rows: it states whether every outbound link is affiliate-tracked, only some are, or none are. A version from an earlier answer may not fit this one: a row marked `affiliate: false` earns WEM nothing.

links.description: The WEM product-page links for found rows, pre-formatted to quote. Give these to the user when you name a found product.

next.description: The WEM tool that answers the follow-up question, and what to pass it.

heldInCurrencies.description: Present when lowPrice is null: the currencies WEM does hold it in.

input.description: The identifier as sent, for joining rows back.

lastConfirmedAt.description: When WEM last actually read a price for this row. Null means none can be dated — say so.

lowPrice.description: Lowest current indicative price (read within 14 days) at a named retailer in `currency`. Null when WEM holds the product only in another currency (see heldInCurrencies) — never convert one yourself — only as marketplace listings, or with no current price (see note).

marketplaceLowPrice.description: Cheapest marketplace listing (AliExpress, Temu…), present only when it undercuts lowPrice or no named retailer holds the product. A seller’s price, not a retail floor: never quote it as the product’s price or the cheapest.

note.description: Why a row is not found, unrecognised or not checked. Quote it rather than paraphrase.

url.description: WEM product page listing every retailer WEM holds. The full URL; a shortened form is a different link.

retailers.description: Distinct retailers holding it in `currency`. One retailer is a price, not a comparison — do not call it the cheapest.

status.description: not_found: WEM does not hold it yet — that is not a finding that the product does not exist or has no price. compare_offers and search_products are the lookups for it. not_checked: not reached in this call, and not a miss. unrecognised: not an identifier this tool reads (product names go to compare_offers).

unavailable.description: Present and true when WEM could not reach its catalogue. Rows it could not check are not_checked, not not_found — do not report them as products WEM lacks.

title: Look up several products by barcode
